issues.description: The getter name for the StockIngredient.name field differs between the template and the solution. In the template repository StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient() in the template calls getIngredientName(). In the solution repository StockIngredient exposes getName(), and the solution's Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact names, so this mismatch across artifacts can confuse students about the expected getter name and required method to call.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the ingredient name across artifacts. Either rename the template getter to getName() and update its usages (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) or change the solution to use getIngredientName(). Also update the problem statement example or instructions to mention the chosen getter name (or state naming is flexible) to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name is named differently between template and solution: the template defines getIngredientName() while the solution defines getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not prescribe exact getter names, which leaves ambiguity. This mismatch can create unnecessary confusion when students try to map the requirement to the provided code (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient in template calls getIngredientName(), while the solution's Stock.findStockIngredient calls getName()).

Update the template to match the intended final API (or update the solution to match the template) and clarify in the problem statement that getters should follow the chosen naming convention (e.g., getName()).
